intro: This isn't graded. Your answers decide where your lessons start, and your seed gets planted either way.

items.prompt: Smaller values go left and larger values go right. Where would 18 be inserted?

options.feedback: 18 < 50, 18 < 30, 18 < 20, so it becomes the left child of 20.
18 is smaller than 20, so it goes left, not right.
18 < 50, so the search goes left at the root and never reaches 70.
18 < 30, so the search goes left at 30, away from 40.

items.prompt: Smaller values go left and larger values go right. Where would 42 be inserted?

options.feedback: 42 > 30, so at 30 the search goes right, not left.
42 < 50, 42 > 30, 42 > 40, so it becomes the right child of 40.
42 < 50, so the search goes left at the root. Checking only the parent misses this.
42 < 50, so it belongs in the left subtree.

items.prompt: In a tree, what is a leaf?

options.feedback: The top node is the root.
Yes: a leaf has no children.
A node with children is internal, however many it has.

items.prompt: What is the height of a tree with only a root?

options.feedback: Counting levels, a lone root is one level. (Some books count edges and say 0.)
There is only one node, so only one level.

items.prompt: Binary search halves the remaining items each step. Roughly how many steps for 1 000 000 items?

options.feedback: That would be √n. Halving is much faster.
That is n/2, the cost of scanning half a list.
